In the Chinese tech community—both in day-to-day discussions and in formal technical documentation—it is standard practice to retain well-established English terms like Token as they are. Additional quantitative evidence from a long-running Linux setup (Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, opencode 1.18.16, provider `opencode`, model `big-pickle`, no custom provider options).

Aggregating `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, `AI_APICallError: Internal server error` from `providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle` occurred **409 times**.

**By day (UTC):**

| Date | Count |
|------|-------|
| 2026-07-22 | 34 |
| 2026-07-23 | 64 |
| 2026-07-24 | 172 |
| 2026-07-27 | 130 |
| 2026-07-28 | 4 |
| 2026-08-11 | 1 |

**By agent (main path, `small=false`):**

- build: 241
- plan: 135
- compaction: **18** (not mentioned in the original report — `/compact` also fails, leaving sessions to grow unbounded)
- explore: 6
- general: 4

Behavior matches the report exactly: 3-6 `stream error` entries followed by new `stream` retries per message; when retries are exhausted the response is silently dropped with no error surfaced to the user. It correlates with degraded backend periods (heavy on Jul 24 and Jul 27), so it appears to be server-side on the opencode provider, and it is **still occurring** as of 2026-08-11 (opencode 1.18.16).

The `compaction` agent being affected (18 occurrences) is an additional data point: failed compactions never complete and the session context keeps growing. Worth tracking alongside the silent-drop behavior.

- #36020: Subagent Read tool returns an attachment but it is not assembled as `image_url` + base64 for openai-compatible vision models

The specific detail here (stale DashScope OSS signed URL returned instead of base64 bytes) may point to a distinct caching bug, but the underlying image pipeline issue in the openai-compatible provider path appears shared.

Thanks for the pointers — I did a control experiment before deciding on duplicate vs distinct, and the results narrow the root cause further:

**Experiment: read a copy of the same image under a fresh, never-before-seen filename (`img_58331.jpg`).**

The `read` tool returned a **different** URL — this time opencode's **own** OSS bucket, not DashScope's:

```

**Conclusion:** this is **not** a filename-keyed caching bug. Every signed URL produced by the read-tool image pipeline for this openai-compatible (DashScope) provider is dead on arrival — stale/invalid signature, redacted object key. Direct base64 `image_url` upload to the same provider works perfectly and returns an accurate description.

**One additional risk worth carrying over to the parent issue:** when the vision model receives these dead URLs, it does **not** error — it silently **hallucinates** a plausible description of the image (in our case, twice, with two entirely different fabricated contents). This makes the failure mode worse than a hard error, since users can't tell the image was never delivered.

```

The root cause is still exactly as described here: in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts`, local (non-`--attach`) mode hardcodes the MIME type:

```ts
const mime = !args.attach
  ? isDirectory
    ? "application/x-directory"
    : "text/plain"          // <- FSUtil.mimeType(path) result on the line above is discarded
  : content && text !== undefined && Buffer.from(text, "utf8").equals(content)
    ? "text/plain"
    : detected
```

`FSUtil.mimeType()` (mime-types `lookup()`) already returns `image/png` correctly for the same path — the value just never gets used in local mode.

Two fix PRs (#34319, #34369) were closed unmerged; the bug has been open since 2025 (#16723, #24698, #25353, #38952). Suggested one-line fix:

```ts
const mime = isDirectory ? "application/x-directory" : detected
```
